Steam Linux 53.16 Adventure barter source reconstruction
Image: /home/lulika/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/Dwarf Fortress/dwarfort
ELF build ID: bcc6789e6fb477b785a2b02be80b8b1b054ff88c

elf-decompiled.c is actual Ghidra 12.1.2 C output for all 14 unwind
procedures in elf-functions.tsv. The shared DecompileJournalEvents.java
manifest reader gives analysis functions its journal_source_ name prefix;
these names do not describe the original game's function roles.
elf-*.asm retains every instruction in each original procedure, including
GCC remote branches. elf-branches.tsv, elf-calls.tsv, elf-literals.tsv and
elf-switches.tsv retain original conditions, direct callees, literal operands
and all signed relative jump-table entries. SIMD/immediate operands are
fragments; adjacent rodata blocks are not null-terminated UI strings.
decompiled-productions.tsv gives reconstructed complete displayed messages
and their Chinese text, including the existing shared translations.

Native barter object offsets (relative to its own start):
  +8 merchant, +10 your_trader, +18 zone, +20 conversation;
  +28 personal, +29 demand_only, +2a strong_affiliation_bonus;
  +2e8 two item filters, +328 two entering-filter flags;
  +32a talkline, +330/+334 maximum currency, +338/+33c offered currency;
  +340 entering item quantity, +341 entering asked currency,
  +342 entering offered currency, +348 editable amount;
  +370 big_announce rows, +388 scroll position.

15d4900 renderer:
  entering item quantity -> Trade how many? (0-MAX), then editable amount;
  entering asked currency -> Ask for how much? (0-MAX), then editable amount;
  entering offered currency -> Offer how much? (0-MAX), then editable amount;
  demand_only -> (Select an item to demand);
  otherwise talkline == -1 -> existing big_announce reply rows;
  otherwise wrap the complete quoted talkline at screen_width-18.
The 37-way selector is retained at 21997d8 / dispatch 15d8e14:
  0: personal -> What did you have in mind?
     otherwise strong affiliation -> An honored visitor! What would you like?
     otherwise -> Greetings. Let's trade.
  7: zone -> Ah, wonderful. Thank you for your business.
     no zone -> That seems fair. You have yourself a deal.
  18,19,20: ethical refusal (death/living creature/tree);
  21: cannot afford; 22: more goods needed; 23: counteroffer;
  29: uncaged living creature; 30: gift accepted;
  31,32: burden/cost refusals; 33: loss refusal;
  34: zone -> Yes, and trade we will! ...
      no zone -> I'm confused. Did you want something?
  35: selected requested goods without an offer;
  36: offered goods without selecting requested goods;
  1..6,8..17,24..28 and out-of-range values: original empty quoted body.
Empty native bodies contain no words; their quotation marks remain native.

15cfd50 artifact refusals:
  personal artifact claim with no relinquishment timestamp -> personal treasure;
  family claim with no relinquishment timestamp -> family heirloom;
  member of entity type 10 or 13 and entity claim with no relinquishment
  timestamp -> treasure of ENTITY.
Personal and entity replies prepend capitalized b676a0 speaker + ': ' when
big_announce is empty, otherwise append the original blank separator.
The family producer explicitly prepends that speaker. Its body-only catalog
form also allows the same typed artifact clause to be composed independently.
All three use a0d8c0 flags=0 and submit the complete source to 423910,
width=68. The existing paragraph hook retains source and native row addresses.

a0d8c0 artifact field:
  unresolved ID -> an unknown artifact;
  resolved name -> language_name English=true;
  unnamed book / written object -> Untitled;
  other unnamed item -> complete e68020 item description;
  flag bit 2 wraps LPAGE markup, but barter callers pass 0.
The runtime uses the existing artifact/book/item/body-component/copy grammar
for this whole field. b676a0 speakers use the existing formatter-owned unit
identity, including caste, profession, curse and authored names/roles.
a278f0 entities retain the existing complete entity-name grammar and unknown
civilization fallback. Names from the supplied screenshot are not dictionary
entries. Typed speaker matching retries colon boundaries before an artifact
title or authored role can be consumed as part of the speaker.

15cd540 transfer/return producer:
  first acknowledgement includes the capitalized merchant speaker;
  subsequent acknowledgements use the existing separator and omit the speaker;
  10226b0, with topic=19 and a returned incident ID, supplies a complete
  memory/reaction prefix; the prefix may be empty;
  personal claim -> Thank you for returning my treasure.;
  family claim -> Thank you for returning my family's treasure.;
  entity claim -> Thank you for returning this treasure to ENTITY.;
  primordial quest -> Thank you for returning this primordial remnant to ENTITY.;
  rescue quest -> Thank you for rescuing this treasure!;
  copied written work -> It's not the original, but we can hope the writing
                         was copied faithfully.
Personal/family/entity acknowledgements can occur in the same complete source.
Fixed-ending catalog forms therefore accept the entire earlier reaction and
acknowledgements as one typed body, translated through the existing complete
announcement grammar; each prefix is shorter than the enclosing message.
The shared native decompiler outputs are:
  ../announcement-conversation/elf-dialogue-10226b0.c
  ../announcement-conversation/elf-memory-events.c (101b7f0, topic 19)
  ../announcement-conversation/elf-dialogue-1016060.c (incident narrative)
Their native dispatch/field branches remain owned by the existing complete
conversation, memory and incident grammars rather than a new list of names.

15cb080 transaction rewards:
  You receive ITEM_LIST to conclude the transaction.
  Native item lists use comma and 'and' joins, complete e68020 labels and
  optional quantity data. This existing adventure-announcement production
  remains in adventure-announcements.tsv, using the shared {i} list grammar.

Other renderer text and dynamic sources:
  Ask for currency / Offer currency / Cannot trade currency;
  You are asking for / You are offering: separate native numbers and 0x0f;
  merchant heading plus (Owes you AMOUNT[0x0f]) or (You owe AMOUNT[0x0f]);
  Trade / Show / Give / Demand, Mark all / Unmark all, You;
  two independent filter strings and their original editing cursor;
  native item-type headings, whole item captions and container captions;
  Contains COUNT item(s), Weight: NUMBER[weight glyph].
The current shared item/creature/material grammar owns all dynamic inventory
labels. Currency/quantity entries retain the original amounts; the debt
caption uses the Unicode equivalent of the native 0x0f currency glyph (☼).
User-entered filter/amount strings, underscores, dots and other native marks
are data or controls, not additional translatable dialogue.
